title: Pskov Court Bars Yabloko From Regional Assembly Race
text: Pskov Court Bars Yabloko From Regional Assembly Race Aug. 26, 2026 @pskovyabloko / Telegram A judge in the western Pskov region has disqualified the liberal Yabloko party’s list of candidates from the upcoming regional assembly elections, the party said on Tuesday evening. The regional ban follows Russia’s Supreme Court ruling last week to reject Yabloko’s final appeal against a nationwide ban barring its candidate list from the State Duma elections next month. Like the lawsuit that led to Yabloko’s federal ban, the Pskov region lawsuit was filed by the small nationalist party Rodina, which claimed Yabloko committed technical violations during its campaign registration. The Pskov Regional Court ruled in favor of Rodina, effectively stripping Russia’s only registered party campaigning on a pro-peace platform from its final remaining stronghold. Pskov was the last of three regions where Yabloko held seats in regional assemblies and had secured ballot access for next month’s elections, according to the outlet 7x7. news Russian Supreme Court Rejects Yabloko’s Appeal Over Candidate List Ban Read more Regional election commissions previously rejected Yabloko’s registration in St. Petersb

title: 3 Killed in Russia as Ukraine Sets Wildberries Warehouse and Oil Refinery Ablaze
text: 3 Killed in Russia as Ukraine Sets Wildberries Warehouse and Oil Refinery Ablaze Aug. 26, 2026 A fire burning at a Wildberries warehouse in the city of Kotovsk, Tambov region. @exilenova_plus / Telegram At least three people were killed in drone attacks across Russia on Wednesday as Ukraine struck and set fire to a Wildberries warehouse in the central Tambov region, the second time the facility has been targeted since July, as well as an oil refinery further to the east. Tambov region Governor Yevgeny Pervyshov said the blaze “completely” destroyed the Wildberries facility in the city of Kotovsk. One worker sustained a concussion from the blast wave, the governor said initially, only later to add that a second person was injured. Wildberries said it safely evacuated all of its employees from the warehouse. It did not comment on the extent of the damage to the facility. Videos and photos shared on social media showed a large column of black smoke rising from the warehouse and spreading across the morning sky in Kotovsk. title: Vedomosti: Leonid Slutsky may lose post as head of international affairs committee in new State Duma

Sources in the State Duma and people close to Russia’s Presidential Administration told the Russian business daily Vedomosti that United Russia wants to regain control of one of the chamber’s key committees. The new committee chair could be Pyotr Tolstoy, currently the State Duma’s deputy speaker from United Russia, the sources said. They named Vyacheslav Nikonov, the committee’s first deputy chair, as a another, though less likely, candidate. Slutsky, who has led the international affairs committee since 2016, will stay on as head of the LDPR faction in the new Duma, according to the sources. A final decision on the committees’ structure and membership won’t come until after the election, the sources said. Several female journalists from the parliamentary press pool publicly accused Leonid Slutsky of harassment in 2018. A parliamentary ethics commission found no violations in his conduct, and Slutsky, who never admitted guilt, ignored calls to leave the State Duma. title: Wildberries warehouse in Russia completely destroyed in Ukrainian drone attack
text: A Wildberries logistics center in Kotovsk, in Russia’s Tambov region, burned to the ground after a Ukrainian drone strike overnight on August 26, Tambov Governor Yevgeny Pervyshov said. Two people were injured in the attack, he said — a 19-year-old man who suffered a concussion and a 49-year-old woman who broke a finger. According to Pervyshov, 19 drones targeted the warehouse in all. Air defenses shot down 16 of them, while three managed to strike the building. Kotovsk Mayor Alexey Plakhotnikov had earlier urged residents to limit “active movement around the city” for the next two days and keep their windows closed because of the heavy fire, smoke, and smog. This marks the second Ukrainian attack on the Kotovsk warehouse. The previous strike occurred overnight on July 18 and killed seven Wildberries employees. Households and businesses have added 2.1 trillion rubles ($25.3 billion) to their cash holdings so far this year. That marks the largest increase recorded since the start of the war, surpassing the 1.8 trillion rubles ($21.7 billion) added between January and August 2023. Back then, cash demand was driven by Russians fleeing the country amid military mobilization, panic during the short-lived Wagner mutiny and, reportedly, off-the-books payments to mercenaries fighting in Ukraine. According to projections by Sberbank, Russia’s largest lender, cash in circulation could rise by 3.8 trillion rubles ($45.8 billion) over the course of 2026, making it the largest annual increase on record. title: Moscow to Summon Romanian Envoy After Russian Diplomat Expelled Over Drone Incursions
text: Moscow to Summon Romanian Envoy After Russian Diplomat Expelled Over Drone Incursions Aug. 26, 2026 Fragments of drones downed on Romanian territory are displayed at the Romanian Foreign Ministry in Bucharest. Romanian Foreign Ministry / via REUTERS Russia’s Foreign Ministry announced plans to summon Romania’s chargé d’affaires in Moscow, the Interfax news agency reported Wednesday. According to the ministry’s short statement, Liliana Burda was expected to be summoned on Thursday. The Russian ministry did not publicly confirm plans to summon Burda or the reason for her planned summoning as of publication. title: Russians Are Rushing for Cash. Should the Kremlin Be Worried?
text: Russians Are Rushing for Cash. Should the Kremlin Be Worried? By Moscow Times Reporter Aug. 26, 2026 A mural painting of a bank in Moscow. Yaroslav Chingaev / Moskva News Agency As the Kremlin prepares to roll out its latest financial innovation — the digital ruble — Russians are increasingly turning to a more old-fashioned alternative: cash. Households and businesses have added 2.1 trillion rubles ($25.3 billion) to their cash holdings so far this year. That marks the largest increase recorded since the start of the war, surpassing the 1.8 trillion rubles ($21.7 billion) added between January and August 2023. Back then, cash demand was driven by Russians fleeing the country amid military mobilization, panic during the short-lived Wagner mutiny and, reportedly, off-the-books payments to mercenaries fighting in Ukraine. According to projections by Sberbank, Russia’s largest lender, cash in circulation could rise by 3.8 trillion rubles ($45.8 billion) over the course of 2026, making it the largest annual increase on record.
